title: Knowledge check: API Rate Limiting and Throttling

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed for “API Rate Limiting and Throttling”?
options: A complete substitute for server-side validation
A guarantee that every database write succeeds atomically
A feature that is always enabled without configuration
questions.explanation: The supplied Django curriculum lists “Rate limits” under lesson 174, “API Rate Limiting and Throttling”. The lesson connects this item to the practical Django workflow for building apis with django.

questions.prompt: Which workflow best supports reliable work on “API Rate Limiting and Throttling”?
options: Copy a production secret into the source file so every environment matches.
Publish an example before checking framework/version compatibility.
Use a documented small example, verify expected behavior, and test an invalid or boundary case.
Assume the browser is trusted and skip server-side checks.
questions.answer_key: Use a documented small example, verify expected behavior, and test an invalid or boundary case.
questions.explanation: Small reproducible examples, server-side validation where relevant, and explicit positive/negative checks help distinguish expected behavior from assumptions. Version, environment, and boundary cases should be documented.

questions.prompt: Which practice is most appropriate when applying “API Rate Limiting and Throttling” in a real application?
options: Expose all internal error messages and credentials to clients.
Validate external input, set timeouts, handle failures, and make retried work idempotent.
Retry every error forever with no backoff or uniqueness check.
Treat a successful HTTP status as proof a remote payment is settled.
questions.answer_key: Validate external input, set timeouts, handle failures, and make retried work idempotent.
questions.explanation: The lesson is part of Building APIs with Django. Select the approach that supports correctness, safe handling of failures, and verifiable behavior; see the linked official documentation for version-specific details.
